title: Hansel and Gretel: exercises
subtitle: Five exercises on the text
label: Exercises
review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: Hansel and Gretel's family was very rich.
Hansel dropped little white pebbles along the path.
The second time, birds ate the bread crumbs.
The roof of the little house was covered with chocolate.
The witch locked Gretel in a cage.
A friendly white horse helped them cross the river.
How did the pebbles show the children the way home?
items.why: “Under the moonlight, the little stones shone brightly.”

items.q: What were the walls of the little house made of?
What did Hansel hold out instead of his finger?
items.why: “But Hansel cleverly held out a tiny chicken bone instead.”

items.q: Why did the witch not see the trick?
What did the children find before they left the house?
options: A chest of gold coins and jewels
items.why: “Before leaving, they discovered a chest filled with gold coins and beautiful jewels.”

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: Hansel and Gretel were left in the forest and found a house made of sweets. A wicked witch lived there: she locked Hansel in a cage and wanted to eat him. Gretel pushed the witch into the oven, and the children went home to their father with a treasure.

items.q: How did Hansel find the way home the first time?
items.model: He dropped little white pebbles along the path. Under the moonlight, the stones shone, and the children followed them home.

items.q: Why couldn't the children find their way home the second time?
items.model: Hansel dropped bread crumbs, but hungry birds ate every crumb.
She pretended not to understand how to look inside the oven. When the witch leaned toward it, Gretel pushed her inside and slammed the door. Then she opened Hansel's cage.

items.q: Hansel and Gretel helped each other. How do you help your brother, sister or friend?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the events in the order of the story.
items: Hansel dropped white pebbles along the path
Hungry birds ate the bread crumbs
The children found a house made of sweets
Gretel pushed the witch into the oven
A white duck helped the children cross the river
